incident.title: Customer reports describe an API outage after deployment, but telemetry shows partial degradation
incident.alert_or_symptom: Customer-support reports describe the Public API Gateway as being down following a recent deployment, although platform telemetry continues to record successful requests.

technical_evidence.observation: Some customers describe the digital service as completely down and state that the problem began shortly after the Public API Gateway observability package was deployed.
Of 84,600 API requests between 19:00 and 19:20, 8.7 percent timed out or returned transient gateway errors while 91.3 percent completed successfully.
The API gateway p95 response time increased from a normal baseline of 720 milliseconds to 6.9 seconds. Successful requests continued throughout the affected interval.
Web and mobile synthetic transactions continued to complete, although some experienced elevated latency or transient failure. No interval of complete API unavailability was detected.

An observability-package update was deployed to the Public API Gateway at 18:32. The deployment changed diagnostic logging and tracing instrumentation but was not intended to alter request routing or transaction processing.

The available traces show elevated request duration across several request paths, but no exception, route failure or processing stage consistently associated with the new observability package has been identified.
DNS, load balancing, compute, database, messaging and storage high-level health checks remain successful. Their individual latency contributions have not yet been independently established.

The evidence establishes partial API performance degradation rather than a complete outage. The temporal relationship with the observability deployment does not establish that the deployment caused the incident.

service_impact.user_impact_description: Customers across the United Kingdom and Ireland may experience slow responses or transient API failures, but most requests and digital transactions continue to complete successfully.
service_impact.business_function_affected: Customer-facing digital browsing and transaction requests
service_impact.workaround_description: Customers may succeed by waiting and trying later, but repeated submission of transactional requests is discouraged and no workaround restores normal response performance.

environmental_context: The Public API Gateway is a Tier 1 business-critical platform service.
The gateway remains materially available and continues to process most requests successfully.
The recent deployment changed observability instrumentation rather than intended request-processing behaviour.
No supporting platform has been directly established as failed.

recent_changes.description: A diagnostic logging and tracing update was deployed to the Public API Gateway approximately 28 minutes before the incident was reported.

reported_unknowns: The directly responsible performance bottleneck or technical condition.
Whether the recent observability deployment has any technical relationship to the degradation.
The independently verified latency contribution of the API gateway and its supporting dependencies.
The expected duration and recovery time for normal API performance.
Whether any failed transactional requests created partial records or duplicate-processing risk.
additional_context: No complete outage, data loss, corruption or serious security exposure has been confirmed.
No rollback or production configuration change has been approved.

model_output.incident_summary: The Public API Gateway is experiencing partial performance degradation, with elevated latency and transient errors, but no complete service unavailability has been observed.

severity.rationale: The incident involves partial performance degradation without a complete outage or widespread impact, and there is an available workaround for users to retry their requests.

incident_category.rationale: The evidence indicates partial performance degradation rather than a complete service unavailability or application failure.

affected_area.rationale: The Public API Gateway is the directly affected component, with impacts on dependent services due to its role in processing requests.

routing.rationale: The Network and Edge Team is primarily responsible for the Public API Gateway, while RG-OPS should be involved due to the partial service degradation.
